title: Who's Who: Oskar Veld
summary: Probe machinist whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Oskar Veld (1811–1873) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a probe machinist whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Veld fabricated the first successful tethered probe from nested brass shells designed to fail visibly if crushed. It returned bearing a pale deposit and scratches that did not match its outward travel.
He refused to call those scratches writing, though collectors have published competing alphabets ever since.

For Alderwick readers, Oskar Veld is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
